skill.name: action-item-organizer
skill.description: Extract actionable work from meeting notes, reports, audits, and reviews, then organize it into prioritized markdown checklists.
skill.summary: Turns unstructured documents into prioritized, trackable action item checklists.
skill.author: Joseph OBrien

security_audit.summary: All static findings were adjudicated as false positives. content.value_statement: Important follow-ups are easy to miss in long notes, reports, and audits. This skill extracts tasks, priorities, owners, locations, and estimates into trackable markdown checklists.
actual_capabilities: Extracts actionable tasks from meeting notes, reviews, reports, and audit documents.
Classifies tasks into P0, P1, P2, and P3 priority levels.
Preserves source context, owners, estimates, tracking IDs, and file locations when available.
Builds nested markdown checklists for complex or multi-step work.
Summarizes item counts, estimated effort, and completion progress by priority.
limitations: It depends on the source document for accurate owners, estimates, and deadlines.
It does not connect to project management tools by itself.
It may need human review when priorities conflict or context is missing.
It produces markdown guidance, not automated task creation.

use_cases.title: Convert Meeting Notes
use_cases.description: Turn scattered follow-ups into clear owners, priorities, and next steps after a planning meeting.

use_cases.title: Organize Review Findings
use_cases.description: Convert code review or design review comments into prioritized remediation tasks with source locations.

use_cases.title: Track Audit Remediation
use_cases.description: Group audit findings by severity and produce a checklist that teams can execute and monitor.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Checklist
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with a short document that has clear action items.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the action-item-organizer skill to extract every action item from this document. Group the results by priority and include owners when named.

prompt_templates.title: Add Metadata and Context
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the source includes owners, estimates, files, or issue IDs.
prompt_templates.prompt: Extract action items from this report. Preserve file paths, line numbers, owners, estimates, tracking IDs, and the original reason for each task.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize Ambiguous Work
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the source document mixes urgent and optional work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Organize these notes into P0 through P3 sections. Explain the priority choice in the context field when the source is ambiguous.

prompt_templates.title: Consolidate Multiple Sources
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for advanced planning across reports, notes, and review comments.
prompt_templates.prompt: Combine these documents into one deduplicated action item checklist. Preserve source references and nest dependent tasks under the main deliverable.

output_examples.input: A code review report lists missing authentication, hardcoded credentials, and several performance improvements.
output: A P0 section lists security blockers with owners, estimates, and source files.
A P1 section captures performance work with the reason and expected impact.
A completion summary shows total items and estimated effort.

output_examples.input: Meeting notes mention documentation updates, deployment fixes, and future design ideas.
output: Urgent deployment work is placed before launch-related documentation tasks.
Future ideas are grouped as lower priority items for later planning.
Named owners are preserved and missing estimates are marked for review.

output_examples.input: An audit report contains findings across security, reliability, testing, and documentation.
output: Findings become grouped checklist sections by priority and category.
Each task keeps its rationale so teams understand the remediation goal.
Nested steps break complex fixes into smaller trackable actions.

best_practices: Provide the full source document so the skill can preserve context and dependencies.
Review inferred priorities when the source does not provide severity or urgency.
Keep source references in the checklist so teams can trace each task back to evidence.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for a checklist from partial notes when missing sections contain action items.
Do not remove source context from high-risk tasks or audit findings.
Do not treat inferred owners, estimates, or priorities as final without review.

faq.question: What document types can this skill process?
faq.answer: It works with meeting notes, reports, audits, code reviews, planning documents, and issue summaries.

faq.question: Does it create tickets in external tools?
faq.answer: No. It creates structured markdown checklists that can be copied into another workflow.

faq.question: How does it decide priority?
faq.answer: It uses urgency, impact, blockers, security risk, and source labels to classify items from P0 to P3.

faq.question: Can it keep file paths and line numbers?
faq.answer: Yes. It preserves file locations and line numbers when they appear in the source document.

faq.question: What happens when metadata is missing?
faq.answer: The checklist marks missing owners, estimates, or locations as TBD for later review.

faq.question: Is human review still needed?
faq.answer: Yes. Review the final checklist when priorities are inferred or the source context is incomplete.
